title: Bundled setup context
contract: The manual describes Max for Live as included with Suite and Standard plus the Max for Live add-on, without separate installation. Entitlement/activation/platform failure behavior is not specified.

title: Selected editor application
contract: File & Folder settings can select a specific Max application path instead of bundled editor; changing path takes effect after Live restart, when opening editor launches chosen Max.

title: Device browser surfaces
contract: Core Library Max instruments/effects appear in Instruments, Audio Effects, MIDI Effects and Modulators; Max for Live label includes installed third-party/user devices and MIDI Tools. This is discovery UI, not proof every arbitrary AMXD works.

title: Modulator role
contract: Modulators are documented as controlling Live parameters with modulation signals. Specific mappings, ranges, parameter ownership, timing and device algorithms are not supplied.

title: Preset workflow
contract: Max devices can have supplied presets and user-created/edited presets similar to ordinary device presets. Exact patch-definition versus parameter-state identity and sharing rules remain U.

title: Open device editor
contract: For Max devices, Edit in Max in title-bar context or Show Options launches Max and opens selected device in editor/patcher.

title: Developer edit button context
contract: The manual distinguishes pre-12.2 device-title Edit button from current Edit in Max command. It documents -MaxForLiveDeveloperMode in Options.txt as restoring button functionality. Exact 12.4.3 option parsing/effective restart/default behavior is U.

title: Device Save instance scope
contract: After editing a device, Max File Save updates all instances of the same device in the Set. Meaning of same-device identity versus preset copies, dirty state and atomicity is not established.

title: Device Save As confirmation
contract: Device Save As opens confirmation asking whether changes apply only to edited preset or all instances.

title: Default device save folders
contract: Max device default save location is the User Library folder appropriate to type, including Max Audio Effect and Max MIDI Effect. The chapter does not enumerate the exact folder name for every other type.

title: Separate AMXD references
contract: Max devices are separate AMXD files rather than embedded in Set. Moving/renaming referenced AMXD can break path; File Manager offers location repair. Exact relocation/search/copy behavior remains U.

title: Existing tool editor route
contract: An existing Max for Live MIDI Tool can be a starting point. Selected tool/template Edit button launches Max editor; this tool UI is distinct from current device-title Edit in Max.

title: Tool saving
contract: Max MIDI Tools are saved with patcher File Save or Save As. The device Save all-instances rule is not automatically transferred to tool selections.

title: Tool default folders
contract: Documented default tool directories are ~/Music/Ableton/User Library/MIDI Tools/Max Transformations and .../Max Generators. User Library relocation/platform path resolution remains U.

title: Tool discovery locations
contract: Tools stored in default folders or browser Places appear in corresponding tool dropdowns; elsewhere they are not found by Indexer and do not appear there. Timing, cache invalidation, recursion and ambiguous duplicate resolution are U.

title: Dependencies and device freeze
contract: Max devices may depend on samples, images or other patches. Device freezing packages files needed to use device; it is distinct from Freeze Track. Exact dependency discovery, supported file types, package grammar and portability are not specified.

title: Reference entry points
contract: Max Help Reference opens built-in documentation with a Max for Live category; MIDI Tools guide is routed through category Guides. Availability/documentation versions and full API/object contracts are not captured here.

title: Max Audio Effect documentary role
contract: The named default Max Audio Effect is a starting point dragged from browser into Set for editing. The manual describes incoming chain audio being passed onward to subsequent devices. This documentary default role supplies no measured unity gain, bit identity, channel/latency/bypass law or arbitrary edited-patch behavior.
